name: Afro Sheen and Ultra Sheen

card.summary: Johnson Products' Chicago hair-care lines for Black consumers, with Ultra Sheen for straightened styles and Afro Sheen for natural afros, used to groom and add shine.

quick.overview:
Ultra Sheen and Afro Sheen were hair-care product lines from the Chicago-based Johnson Products Company. Ultra Sheen, from 1957, served women who straightened their hair, and Afro Sheen served the natural-hair styles that rose in popularity with the Black is beautiful movement.

They helped people look groomed by conditioning and adding sheen to textured hair, and the brands became a landmark of Black-owned business and advertising.
quick.how: They were sold as everyday grooming products for styling and finishing textured hair, with Ultra Sheen aimed at straightened hair and Afro Sheen at afros.
quick.risks: No product-specific safety data were gathered here; as with any cosmetic, individual scalp or skin reactions can occur.

lead: Ultra Sheen and Afro Sheen were hair-care brands made by the Johnson Products Company of Chicago, founded in 1954 by George E. Johnson Sr. and his wife Joan with a barber and a $250 loan [1]. Their purpose was grooming: giving textured hair a polished, shiny look in the styles of the era.

Joan Johnson repositioned the Ultra Sheen line for women who straightened their hair in 1957, and by the 1960s the line reportedly held about 80 percent of the Black hair-care market [1]. Afro Sheen became the best-known brand as afros grew popular, and its marketing tied it to racial pride and the Black is beautiful movement [1].

The company also made business history, going public in 1971 as the first African-American-owned company on the American Stock Exchange and sponsoring Soul Train, becoming the first Black-owned company to sponsor a national TV program [1].

chain: Apply conditioning and sheen products to textured hair
angle.text: The products were used to groom and add shine to textured hair, with Ultra Sheen for straightened styles and Afro Sheen for afros.

paras: Johnson Products began with Ultra Wave, a men's hair relaxer sold to barbers in Chicago and New York [1]. Sales reached $40 million annually by 1976, with 500 employees and a factory in Nigeria [1].
After the Johnsons divorced, Joan became chairman and son Eric CEO until 1992; Ivax bought the company in 1993 and Procter & Gamble acquired it in 2004 [1].
Afro Sheen advertising promoted racial pride, and Soul Train sponsorship from 1971 gave the brand a national platform [1].
